composed k is ITSELF a k — closure-identical head [fn_ptr=

noodles/6abfb23:
A forensic pass on the master chain — the new `npm run audit` harness,
which renders through the real buildGraph and measures what the chain
DOES against what its constants claim — found it applying +19.9 dB of
small-signal gain while the code wrote down +5.5. The missing +14.4 came
from three stages that hid it, none of them visible in the source: Web
Audio mandates an automatic makeup on every DynamicsCompressorNode that
no API reports (measured +5.60 on the glue, +6.41 per input comp, +8.55
on the drum parallel); tanh(x*1.2)/tanh(1.2) self-normalizes to +3.16 dB;
and Tone's Distortion wet is an equal-power crossfade of two COHERENT
paths, so wet=0.42 summed to +5.59 dB, not a 42% blend. That phantom gain
is what justified a -20 dB threshold and parked the program on the ceiling
at -4.8 LUFS with a crest of 6.3 — past the loudness-war line, no dynamic
variety left to lose.

The fix is structural. Every stage is unity at the origin by
construction; the only things that move the level are three constants that
say a number out loud. The spec makeup is measured and subtracted
(makeComp); the saturation is our own curve with a real dry/wet mix and a
unity origin slope; the crossfade sums to unity. Measured after: the
per-stage model closes to the full-chain sweep within 0.01 dB.

Tone.Limiter(-2) is deleted. It builds a Compressor and never passes knee,
inheriting Tone's 30 dB default — a "limiter" whose knee spanned -17..+13
dBFS, contributing 0.02 dB for a 6 ms lookahead. The ceiling is now the
whole maximizer and brickwall, and un-oversampled on purpose: a memoryless
curve's own bound IS the sample-peak guarantee only when it isn't
oversampled (a 4x clamp's reconstruction filter rings past the clamp,
measured +0.27 dBFS out of a 0.78 curve). CEIL carries the true-peak
headroom the Bluetooth codecs of use case 2 need.
